expected: Welcome to our newsroom. In this unit, you will learn to identify sources, report what other people said, and describe events in the past. You will explore political and entertainment news, learn the language of natural disasters, and build a clear news bulletin. The people and events in these teaching examples are fictional.

expected: The editor is comparing two photographs of the same bridge. Before sharing a report, she checks who published it, when it was taken, and what the evidence shows. A photograph can provide useful information, but it may need context. An opinion expresses a judgement. A rumour is information that has not been confirmed.

expected: This is a fictional teaching example. A journalist interviews Maya outside the library after a storm. Maya says, "I am worried about the library." The journalist writes down her exact words. This is direct speech. The speaker uses I because she is talking about herself. The quotation preserves the words she actually said.

expected: Later, the journalist tells his editor about the interview. Maya said that she was worried about the library. This is reported speech. expected: In this fictional news story, a council spokesperson discusses repairs to a community library. She says, "We will publish the repair plan tomorrow." Two days later, a journalist reports that the spokesperson said they would publish the repair plan the following day. The journalist should then check whether the plan was actually published. Reporting a promise does not prove that it was fulfilled.

expected: In this fictional interview, a singer announces a community concert. She says, "I can perform on Saturday." Later, the interviewer reports that the singer said she could perform on Saturday. An announcement from the singer is different from an unconfirmed rumour. When discussing entertainment news, explain where the information came from and separate the person's words from your own opinion.

expected: A flood happens when water covers land that is normally dry. In this fictional scene, the river overflowed and flooded a residential street. A rescue crew travelled through the street in a boat. The word flooded describes what happened. The phrase a rescue crew names the people responding. We need a reliable source before reporting numbers or causes.

expected: An earthquake is a sudden shaking of the ground. In this fictional scene, an earthquake damaged several buildings. An assessment team inspected the area from behind a barrier. expected: A drought is a long period with much less rain than a place needs. In this fictional scene, the reservoir has very little water and the ground is dry and cracked. To report a completed event, we could say that water levels fell during the dry season. Fell is the past form of fall.

expected: A hurricane is a powerful tropical storm with strong winds and heavy rain. In this fictional scene, the wind bent the palm trees and rain reduced visibility. expected: This is a fictional news bulletin for language practice. Good evening. A storm hit Greenford on Monday and damaged the community library. We will update this report when more information is confirmed.
